name: Duryodhana
role: Eldest Kaurava prince, rival of the Pandavas
summary: Duryodhana is the eldest of the hundred Kaurava brothers in the Mahabharata and the main rival of the Pandavas. He is also remembered as a skilled mace fighter and a loyal friend, and some places in India worship him.
about: In the Mahabharata, Duryodhana is the eldest son of Dhritarashtra and Gandhari. The Adi Parva calls him a portion of Kali, the spirit of strife, and says that his birth came with troubling omens. He grows up with a deep rivalry towards his cousins, the Pandavas, and is guided by his uncle Shakuni. The epic tells how he trains in the mace with Balarama and gives Karna a kingdom and his friendship. The conflict over the throne leads to the dice game, the Pandavas' exile and finally the Kurukshetra war, in which he chooses Krishna's army over Krishna himself. He is struck down in a mace duel with Bhima, but the epic says he was later seen in splendour in heaven. Writers and performers have shown him in different ways over the centuries, from Bhasa's sympathetic play to temples in Kerala and Uttarakhand.
kidSummary: Duryodhana is the eldest of the hundred Kaurava brothers. He was a mighty mace fighter and a very loyal friend to Karna, but he could not share the kingdom with his cousins, the Pandavas. That led to the big war at Kurukshetra, and in some parts of India he is still honoured today.

story.title: A prince with a hundred brothers
story.text: Duryodhana is born as the eldest of a hundred brothers. He grows up in Hastinapura with his cousins, the five Pandavas.

story.title: A friend for Karna
story.text: When others doubt Karna's right to compete in a contest, Duryodhana makes Karna the king of Anga. The two stay close friends from then on.

story.title: The quarrel over the kingdom
story.text: Duryodhana cannot bear to see Yudhishthira's wealth and fame. After a famous dice game, the Pandavas have to leave for twelve years of exile and one year in hiding.

story.title: Choosing an army
story.text: Before the war, both Arjuna and Duryodhana ask Krishna for help. Duryodhana chooses Krishna's large army, and Arjuna chooses Krishna himself.

story.title: The mace duel
story.text: At the end of the Kurukshetra war, Duryodhana fights Bhima with maces. He falls in the duel, and in the epic's final chapters he is seen in heaven.

teaches: Every person has more than one side
texts: Mahabharata (Adi, Sabha, Udyoga, Shalya and Svargarohana Parvas)
places: Poruvazhy Peruviruthy Malanada Temple, Kollam, Kerala
Temples in the Tons valley, Uttarakhand

facts.text: Duryodhana joins yodhana, fighting, to dur, badly or hard: one who fights badly, or is hard to fight. Scholar David Gitomer says in later plays such as Venisamhara the Pandavas say Suyodhana (fights well) and his side says Duryodhana.

The sage Maitreya urged peace in the exile, but Duryodhana slapped his thigh in scorn, so Maitreya said Bhima would one day break it. In the final duel Krishna reminded Bhima by clapping his own thigh, and Bhima struck Duryodhana's thigh.

The Adi Parva says Duryodhana was born from a part of Kali, the spirit of strife, not the goddess Kali. At his birth he cried like a donkey and donkeys brayed back in the royal stables, which was taken as a bad omen.

Duryodhana tricked King Shalya of Madra, the Pandavas' own maternal uncle, into joining the Kaurava side. In the end he gathered eleven akshauhinis, huge armies, though Balarama declined to take part.
When Duryodhana and Arjuna reached Krishna at Dvaraka, Krishna was pretending to be asleep. When he woke he saw Arjuna first, and then offered the two of them a choice between himself and his army.
Duryodhana is said to have poisoned Bhima, but nagas, serpent beings, cured Bhima and gave him great strength.
He planned to burn the Pandavas in a house made of lac, but they escaped through a secret tunnel.
In the Pandavas' palace at Indraprastha, Duryodhana mistook floors for water and water for floors, and Bhima laughed at him.
A famous line blaming Draupadi for laughing at him at the palace is added by popular retellings and TV, and the epic does not include it.
The Gandharvas once captured him during a trip to the forest, and it was the Pandavas who rescued him.
He refused the Pandavas' peace offer of just five villages, saying he would not give even land the size of a needle's tip.
Duryodhana tried to capture Krishna in his court, and Krishna showed his cosmic Vishvarupa form. Duryodhana still refused to bow.

At the end of the war he hid beneath the surface of a magically fortified lake. When Yudhishthira called to him, he first answered from underwater, then came out and chose Bhima, his old rival, for a last mace duel.
After the war, Yudhishthira found Duryodhana in heaven, in splendour, because he had carried out his warrior duties.
Ashamed after the Gandharva capture, Duryodhana lay down meaning to end his life. Danavas carried him to Patala and told him their penance had made his body above the waist as hard as a diamond.
The Poruvazhy Peruviruthy Malanada temple in Kollam, Kerala, has no idol and no inner shrine. Devotees honour Duryodhana at an open platform.

Local legend at the Kerala temple says Duryodhana wandered there while searching for the Pandavas and gave away hundreds of acres to the temple. The land tax on those fields is said to be still collected in the name of Duryodhanan.
Mythologist Devdutt Pattanaik writes that in Tamil Nadu, devotees of Draupadi make sand images of Duryodhana and jump on its thighs as part of a ritual.
In the Tons valley in Uttarakhand, villagers of Jakhol honour a deity called Samsu, long understood as Duryodhana, though today many call the deity Someshwar, a form of Shiva.

Lying broken after the mace duel, Duryodhana let Ashwatthama take command of what was left of his army. That night Ashwatthama raided the Pandava camp, and the epic says Duryodhana died after hearing his report.

In the Shanti Parva, Narada says Duryodhana carried off the Kalinga king's daughter from her swayamvara with Karna's help. At home he defended it by citing Bhishma's abduction of three Kashi princesses for his half-brother.
Duryodhana trained under Balarama and became his favourite pupil in mace fighting. At a public display, he and Bhima clashed so fiercely that others had to step in and stop them.

quiz.q: Who taught Duryodhana to fight with the mace?
quiz.why: Balarama's favourite mace student was Duryodhana.

quiz.q: What did Duryodhana give his friend Karna?
quiz.why: He crowned Karna king of Anga.

quiz.q: What did Duryodhana choose from Krishna before the war?
quiz.why: He chose the Narayani army, while Arjuna chose Krishna.

quiz.q: How much land did Duryodhana refuse to give the Pandavas?
quiz.why: He said he would not give even land the size of a needle tip.

quiz.q: In which Indian state is there a temple to Duryodhana with no idol?
quiz.why: The Malanada temple near Kollam has no idol.
